s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative infection of a device implant site with signs of local inflammation and possible systemic infection
salient_findings: Inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site
Lesion darkened and enlarged despite antibiotic therapy
key_facts: Dual-chamber pacemaker implantation in the left prepectoral area
Presented with fever on postoperative day 4
Inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site
Swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis
Lesion darkened and enlarged by day 7 despite antibiotic therapy

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal biofilm infection
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of Staphylococcus epidermidis and signs of local inflammation

shortlist.label: Pacemaker pocket infection
shortlist.why_kept: Inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site

shortlist.label: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis infection
shortlist.why_kept: Swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis, potential for resistance

shortlist.label: Abscess formation
shortlist.why_kept: Necrotic lesion and signs of local inflammation

shortlist.label: Sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Fever, elevated inflammatory syndrome, and potential for systemic infection

raw.rationale: The patient presented with an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the pacemaker implant site, which is consistent with a pocket infection, and the presence of Staphylococcus epidermidis in the swab of the lesion supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal biofilm infection
rejected.why: While possible, the presence of a necrotic lesion and the failure of antibiotics suggest a more localized infection like a pocket infection

rejected.label: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis infection
rejected.why: There is no mention of methicillin resistance in the provided information

rejected.label: Abscess formation
rejected.why: Although an abscess could be part of the infection, the term 'pocket infection' more specifically describes the infection's location and nature in relation to the pacemaker

rejected.label: Sepsis
rejected.why: The patient has localized signs of infection and negative blood cultures, which suggests a localized infection rather than sepsis
